items.stem: The length of a table is 47 cm, correct to the nearest centimetre.

parts.t: Write down the lower bound of the length.
Write down the upper bound of the length.

sols: The measurement is correct to the nearest 1 cm, so the true length is within ½ × 1 = 0.5 cm of 47 cm.
half of the unit of accuracy
any length below 47.5 cm rounds down to 47 cm

items.stem: The mass of a parcel is 3.6 kg, correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.t: Write down the lower bound of the mass.
Write down the upper bound of the mass.

A number x is 8.40, correct to 2 decimal places.
Complete the error interval for x.
…………… ≤ x < ……………

sols: 1 decimal place means correct to the nearest 0.1 kg, so the half‑interval is 0.05 kg.
2 decimal places means correct to the nearest 0.01, so the half‑interval is 0.005.
the lower bound is included, the upper bound is not

items.stem:
A crate has a mass of 24 kg, correct to the nearest kilogram.
A lorry is loaded with 8 of these crates.

parts.t: Calculate the upper bound of the total mass of the 8 crates.
Calculate the lower bound of the total mass of the 8 crates.

sols: Each crate has upper bound 24 + 0.5 = 24.5 kg.
The total is largest when every crate is as heavy as possible.
Each crate has lower bound 24 − 0.5 = 23.5 kg.

items.stem:
The diagram shows a rectangle.
Its length is 12.4 cm and its width is 7.8 cm, each correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.t: Calculate the upper bound of the perimeter of the rectangle.

Calculate the upper bound of the area of the rectangle.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: Upper bound of the length = 12.4 + 0.05 = 12.45 cm
Upper bound of the width = 7.8 + 0.05 = 7.85 cm
Upper bound of the perimeter = 40.6 cm
The area is largest when both sides take their upper bounds.
Upper bound of the area = 97.7 cm2 (3 s.f.)

items.stem:
A wooden plank has length 2.4 m, correct to 1 decimal place.
A piece of length 0.85 m, correct to 2 decimal places, is cut from the plank.

parts.t: Calculate the upper bound of the length of wood that is left.
Calculate the lower bound of the length of wood that is left.

sols: Plank: 2.35 ≤ length < 2.45. Piece cut off: 0.845 ≤ length < 0.855.
What is left is largest when the plank is longest and the piece cut off is shortest.
for a subtraction, use the upper bound minus the lower bound
What is left is smallest when the plank is shortest and the piece cut off is longest.

items.stem: A runner runs 480 m, correct to the nearest 10 m, in a time of 32.5 seconds, correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.t:
Calculate the upper bound of the runner's average speed.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Calculate the lower bound of the runner's average speed.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: Speed = distance ÷ time, so the speed is greatest when the distance is greatest and the time is least.
dividing by a smaller number gives a larger answer
The speed is least when the distance is least and the time is greatest.

items.stem:
A metal block has mass 250 g, correct to the nearest gram, and volume 62 cm3, correct to the nearest cubic centimetre.
The density of the block is found using density = mass ÷ volume.

parts.t:
Calculate the upper bound of the density.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Calculate the lower bound of the density.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: The density is greatest for the greatest mass and the smallest volume.
The density is least for the smallest mass and the greatest volume.

items.stem:
A cylinder has radius 4.5 cm, correct to 1 decimal place, and height 12 cm, correct to the nearest centimetre.
The volume of a cylinder is πr2h.

parts.t:
Calculate the upper bound of the volume of the cylinder.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Calculate the lower bound of the volume of the cylinder.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: Every factor is multiplied, so the volume is greatest when both are greatest.
The volume is least when both the radius and the height are least.
ms:
M1 for 4.55 and 12.5 both seen
M1 for π × 4.55² × 12.5
A1

items.stem:
The diagram shows a right-angled triangle.
The two shorter sides are 6.4 cm and 8.2 cm, each correct to 1 decimal place.
The hypotenuse has length h cm.

parts.t:
Calculate the upper bound of h.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

Calculate the lower bound of h.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

sols: The two shorter sides lie in 6.35 ≤ a < 6.45 and 8.15 ≤ b < 8.25.
h = √(a2 + b2), so h is greatest when both shorter sides are greatest.
h is least when both shorter sides are least.
ms:
M1 for 6.45 and 8.25 both seen
M1 for √(6.45² + 8.25²) oe
A1

items.stem:
A cyclist travels 1480 m, correct to the nearest 10 m, in a time of 124.0 seconds, correct to the nearest 0.1 seconds.
The average speed of the cyclist is v m/s.

parts.t:
Calculate the upper bound of v.
Give your answer correct to 4 significant figures.

Calculate the lower bound of v.
Give your answer correct to 4 significant figures.

By comparing your answers to parts (a) and (b), write down the value of v to a suitable degree of accuracy.
Give a reason for your answer.

sols: The speed is greatest for the greatest distance and the least time.
The speed is least for the least distance and the greatest time.
Compare the two bounds digit by digit: 11.98… and 11.89…
To 3 significant figures they are 12.0 and 11.9 — these do not agree.
To 2 significant figures they are both 12.
the upper and lower bounds agree to 2 significant figures, so only 2 significant figures of the answer can be relied on
ms:
B1 for 12 (or 12 m/s)
B1 for a correct reason, e.g. both bounds round to 12 to 2 significant figures oe
FT their (a) and (b)
